name: Central bank stress
value: BoE raised to 4%; yen near 160, no intervention
summary: Central banks tighten against energy-driven inflation; Japan warns on the yen near 160 but has not intervened
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and projects inflation peaking near 5% in mid-2027, a policy reversal driven by higher energy prices (Bank of England). Japan's finance minister Katayama warned of one-sided yen moves near 160 per dollar on 13 Nov and said Tokyo would coordinate with the US Treasury, after vice finance minister Mimura cautioned on 12 Nov (investingLive; NST). No new intervention, emergency move or challenge to a central-bank head was found as of 24 Nov, so this stays a stagflationary dilemma at Watch.
for_you: Rising policy rates feed through to mortgage and loan costs over time. Borrowers on variable or soon-to-expire fixed rates are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma (BoE hiking with CPI seen near 5%); no G7 intervention, emergency move or attempt to remove a head

sources.title: Bank of England — Monetary Policy Report, November 2026

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
